title: The 3,915-line map surface the user draws on is imported by no test, and three standing fixes live inside it.
detail: Two enumerations agree: an import grep over every test file is empty (exit 123), and a bare-token grep finds 22 test files that mention it and none that load it. Cause stated by the repo itself at src/renderer/components/__tests__/map-escape.test.ts:6.

title: 170 test harnesses exist and none is run by the test suite, the landing script, or CI; there is no CI.
detail: Verified against the literal test and land script bodies. No .github tracked or on disk; gh run list returns zero runs while authenticated. An intermediate controller count of 5 reachable was a substring artifact and is withdrawn; the figure is zero.

title: 24 CDP harnesses attach to whatever page holds their port instead of refusing, so a failed launch reads a stranger's screen back as a measurement.
detail: 155 files carry a PORT default across 75 distinct ports; 134 of 156 carry a portFree preflight. The 24 without one attach via list.find(t => t.type === 'page' && t.webSocketDebuggerUrl) with no check that the page belongs to the child they spawned. Controller re-derived the count independently after a false zero from zsh word-splitting.

title: Appending a block through the art path leaves an interior range of the collision index zero-filled.
detail: out.set(src) covers only src.length (410 for GHZ) and the append loop writes from doc.blocks.length (439) up, so 410-438 stay zero. collision-write.ts:694 says so in its own words. The shrink direction and the collision door are both closed; this is the open half of the prior packet's U6.

title: A save staleness guard only runs when the caller passes an optional argument; omitting it silently restores the bug the guard was written against.
detail: classic-save.ts:101 declares gen?: DomainGen and the guard reads if (atGen && ...). One producer passes it today. Controller-verified.

title: Eight harnesses select on UI wording the app retired, so they fail the moment anyone runs them.
detail: Booked as one harness; measured as eight carrying only the old vocabulary, verified as live selectors rather than comments. 15 files carry old, 16 new, 7 both.

title: No harness records which revision of a sibling repo it ran against, so a stale fixture is indistinguishable from a current one.
detail: Only 4 of ~156 harness files call git rev-parse at all. ABSENT is handled well fleet-wide; STALE is the blind spot.

title: A plain build reads as FRESH to every instrument in the repo, then the harness dies because the debug hooks are absent.
detail: VITE_AURORA_DEBUG=1 leaves no mark on the file the freshness guard stats, so build flavour is a fourth state collapsed into FRESH.

title: The shared collision module set has never been read by a reviewer, and has taken 3,010 new lines and six new files since the last sweep.
detail: The August packet recorded it as the aeon/s4 system, which is false and is why all 18 seats skipped it: collision-adapter.ts:12 declares an interface and classic renderer code imports it directly. Its dense test suite was written by the parcels that wrote the code, so it is an author's tests, not an audit. Controller corrected the seat's claim that the file list was unchanged: 14 files then, 20 now.

title: The claim that the ROM resolves overhang blocks from the adjacent zone's table is unverified and Aurora cannot check it.
detail: Seat evidence only, never checked, needs cross-file reach the editor does not have. The zero-fill behaviour is real and booked separately; the reason it is a bug is not established. Both sides are recorded at the site.

title: The booked claim that every harness defaults to the same debug port is false in both halves.
detail: 75 distinct ports across 155 files; 134 of 156 refuse an occupied port rather than attaching. The generalisation came from one night's two-file collision. The narrow real finding is HARNESS-PORT-NO-PREFLIGHT.

title: The label calling the shared collision module set the aeon/s4 backend is false, and it is the sentence that caused a whole subsystem to go unaudited.
detail: Adapter-based; s4 is one implementation; classic renderer code imports it directly. Re-inheriting the label will reproduce the gap.

title: Only half of the collision-index overhang defect was closed; the art path still zero-fills.
detail: Shrink direction closed in s1-io.ts (replacing a gate that was literally bytesEqual(x.slice().slice(), x), true for every input); collision door closed at 4de2e617. Tracked open as COLIND-ART-PATH-ZEROFILL.

title: The last sweep's zero-runtime-coverage gap is closed as capability and open as a gate: 67 aeon-driving harnesses exist and none runs automatically.
detail: 60 registered as harness scripts, running against freshly cloned aeon fixtures. Do not re-open 'aeon has no runtime coverage'; the live row is that all of it sits outside npm test with no CI.

title: The last sweep's unaudited-subsystem gap is still open and needed re-chartering before it could be closed.
detail: Tracked as COLLISION-NEVER-AUDITED; a seat is reading it in this sweep's first wave.

title: A harness run from an isolated copy silently drove the main checkout's build, so three measurements including a baseline were of the wrong tree.
detail: ELECTRON_BIN names one FILE, not a tree; a worktree without node_modules fails isRunnableTree and the walk borrows the main checkout's dist/. Caught only by a planted mutation printing PASS against an unmutated app. It DOES announce it (borrowed: true), so this is says-unread rather than silent, and the fix is a reader. The standing dispatch brief now carries AURORA_BUILT_TREE beside ELECTRON_BIN.

title: Aurora has no continuous integration of any kind, so nothing runs on push.
detail: No .github tracked or on disk; gh run list returns zero runs while authenticated, exit status checked on gh itself. Stated as a property that holds rather than a defect: it means a peer lane's CI-only-guard failure mode cannot occur here, while making HARNESS-NEVER-RERUN the sharper exposure.

title: When the editor refuses a typed value, the explanation is more than twice as tall as the box it is painted in.
detail: 280px of content in a 129px scroller, over the app's own EW-LAYER-CARD-SCROLLER bar, on every refusal on that surface. Composed at refusal time by NumberField, so no static census could see it. Still 280-in-129 at 1680x2200, so not a small-window artifact. Found by the row-remap harness parcel and left red on purpose as harness row [5b2].

title: An unreadable or malformed project sidecar is silently overwritten at project open, destroying every hand-written override before any UI renders.
detail: Every link controller-verified at the pin. A read failure (s1/index.ts:295), invalid JSON (mapping.ts:59) and a non-object root (mapping.ts:62) all collapse to config:{} — INDISTINGUISHABLE from 'no sidecar' (mapping.ts:53). SidecarState carries only {config, issues} and no rejected flag. The object is truthy, so `if (sidecar && bridge.writeSidecar)` passes; seedClassicBuildConfig({}) fills all three keys and returns changed:true (mapping.ts:134-143); ipcClassicBridge.writeSidecar (classic-bridge.ts:61) writes via writeBinaryFile — an UNGUARDED write, no mtime conflict check. writeSidecar has ZERO test coverage (grep over every test file, exit 123). Repro needs no harness: put a trailing comma in .aurora/project.json, open the project, cat the file. THE CORRECT GUARD ALREADY EXISTS ONE DIRECTORY OVER: the canvas path carries sidecarRejected with the rule stated in its own comment — a sidecar Aurora could not READ is one it must not overwrite. Second writer with the same flaw: ProjectSetupTab.tsx:188-191 via Setup then Apply.

title: A second save staleness guard is skipped when its optional argument is omitted, and it also suppresses the warning toast.
detail: atGen?: number at canvasStore.ts:175 with `atGen !== undefined && ...` at :330: absent means stale=false, the doc clears AND returns true, so canvas-save.ts:125 suppresses the warning too. One producer today (canvas-save.ts:64). Sibling of the booked SAVE-GEN-OPTIONAL; the classic one is the more arming of the two because its `collect` is an injectable parameter, so a second producer needs no new call site.

title: A composer document with unsaved strokes is closed with an info toast and no confirmation.
detail: Three sites call useArtStore.getState().closeDocument() directly, bypassing closeDocumentGuarded. The strokes live only in artStore.open.doc and no registered saver can write them. Mitigating: the target tile genuinely no longer exists, so there is nowhere to save to — which is an argument for confirming, not for closing silently.

title: A dirty composer document shows no tab dot and does not enable Save, and one open path can become unexitable except by discarding.
detail: currentDirtySnapshot has no artDirty field though currentOpenDirtySnapshot does. No data is lost — the close and open guards both use the other snapshot. Second-order: with only artDirty set, Save-and-open runs the savers, re-snapshots still dirty and aborts forever, and openBlockedMessage names only the canvas case.

title: A drag in progress survives a keyboard act switch and writes the old act's coordinates into an unrelated object in the new one, once per mouse move and outside undo.
detail: Controller-verified links: App.tsx:159 is a WINDOW keydown (key 1-9, no shift/alt) calling requestFocusIndex, so no pointer event is involved; the level pane at App.tsx:273 is an UN-KEYED div that only toggles display, so MapViewport is never remounted; getSectionByIndex resolves the act fresh at call time. Two damages: per-mousemove writes to section.objects[index].x/y with bumpLiveEdit and no command at all, and then finishGesture writes act A's start coordinates into act B's object through a real move-object command, losing act A's move. THE CURE IS ALREADY IN THIS FILE ON THE OTHER AXIS: endGuideDrag carries a witness (JSON.stringify(layer) !== drag.witness -> return, MapViewport.tsx:2450) whose docblock states the rule. dragTarget, paintStroke.sectionIndex, marqueeDragStart.sectionIndex and bandStamp all carry a bare index with no witness. And App.tsx:312 keys the CANVAS pane by document with a comment naming in-flight gestures as the reason; the level pane is the one surface that skipped it.

title: A tab switch that changes facet unmounts the map mid-stroke, so the paint is already written into the document but no command is ever recorded.
detail: LevelWorkspace.tsx:63-65 runs switchFacet in an effect keyed on the active tab, changing the component type and unmounting MapViewport. The window-mouseup effect's cleanup removes listeners only and never calls finishGesture, so the release never commits. This is the state MapViewport.tsx:2189-2192 says was fixed for the mouseleave route; the unmount route was not closed. A second no-pointer trigger is MapViewport.tsx:1835, switchFacet('art') from the keydown handler itself.

title: Ctrl+Delete and Alt+Backspace destroy the selected object, because the only data-destroying key branch sits above the guard that exists to stop modified keys.
detail: Controller-verified: the Delete/Backspace branch at :1869 tests no modifier at all, and the hoisted guard `if (e.ctrlKey || e.metaKey || e.altKey) return;` is 54 lines BELOW it at :1923, where its own comment claims it covers ALL modified keys. Three other dispatches also escape it: 's' at :1805 tests ctrl/meta but not alt, so Alt+S opens a document and switches facet; F7 at :1850 checks nothing; Ctrl/Cmd+C and V at :1758/:1789 have no alt exclusion.

title: The map's wheel handler calls preventDefault in a passive React listener, so it never suppresses the browser's own zoom, and the repo already ruled on this elsewhere.
detail: React 19 registers root wheel listeners as passive. use-anchored-zoom.ts:11-12 states the rule and does it correctly with a native non-passive listener; MapViewport uses neither that helper nor a native listener, and handleWheel never gates on ctrlKey.

title: A background stroke on the act default committed after an act switch lands on the new act's plane, indexed by the old act's tiles.
detail: endBgStroke passes bgRef and a freshly read level. history.ts:71-74 resolves a library bgRef by id, which is safe across a switch, but the bgRef===null branch falls back to level.act.bgLayout. The project reasoned this through for UNDO timing (its docblock says so) and never applied it to COMMIT timing. MapViewport.tsx:2631 also mixes stale entries with a freshly read activeSectionIndex in one command.

title: The map canvas ignores device pixel ratio, so its backing store is truncated to whole pixels and stretched, and hit-testing drifts toward the far edge.
detail: A grep for devicePixelRatio over the file exits 1, a genuine zero with stderr unsuppressed. canvas.width = rect.width truncates because canvas.width is an unsigned long, while the element is styled 100%/100%. screenToWorld divides by zoom with no compensation. On HiDPI the pixel-art surface renders at half resolution.

title: Warping before the mouse has ever entered the map treats never-hovered as hovered at the top-left corner.
detail: lastMouse is initialised to {x:0,y:0} and F7 warps to screenToWorld of it, so a cold F7 warps to the world point under screen 0,0 instead of refusing. Absent and at-the-corner are the same value.

title: The collision grid an agent reads labels column 100 identically to column 0, on the surface whose stated purpose is that agents read data rather than screenshots.
detail: Controller-reproduced with the source expressions: the tens row is floor((x+c)/10) % 10 and prints a space for 0, so x=100 and x=0 emit byte-identical rulers while x=120 reads as 20. Sections are 128 cells wide and validation.ts accepts any x with x+w <= 128. Row labels are correct; only the column axis caps. The single ruler test uses x=9,w=3 — the one case a two-digit ruler gets right, so it could not have failed.

title: Two collision paint functions have no live callers while their docblocks name them as the agent tool's core in the present tense, and neither can express a crossover span.
detail: Every non-test hit is a comment. The live agent path is agent-handler.ts:491/497 via the both-planes functions; the human path goes through buildBothPlanesEntries directly. The consequence is not cosmetic: collisionRectCells is called with no span argument so it always defaults to 'cell', a width that layer-transition.ts:226-234 proves always nets to nothing for a two-way pair, so a reader modelling the tool from the function its own docblock names gets the span semantics backwards.

title: A loader derives a plane's bound from the very array being bounded, which the consumer module explicitly forbids.
detail: collision-cell-resolve.ts:41-44 says call sites must never pass an array's own length, because deriving the bound from the data being bounded is how a short plane stays short. load.ts:380 passes baseline.length. Not live today because the arrays are allocated at exactly SECTION_PLANE_WORDS, so the number is right for a reason the call site does not state.

title: The crossover audit truncates to the shorter plane and reports ok for an absent one, with no mismatch signal.
detail: Math.min over the two plane lengths, an early return of zero cells for a null plane, and a severity function that never consults the cell count. Its sibling resolvePlaneWords reports a length fault loudly; this one is silent. Not reachable from today's loader, and reported because this audit is the only place a self-mark is noticed anywhere.

title: The never-audited collision subsystem was read in full for the first time and is substantially correct, including flip maths checked against the engine's own bake.
detail: All 20 files read. The flip functions are byte-identical to aeon's collision_pipeline.py at a pinned revision, verified by the seat rather than assumed. The single non-involution (0xF0 -> 0x10) is faithful to the ROM's own bake, chased as a candidate headline finding and recorded so nobody re-chases it. Five of the six new modules are correct; the sixth carries the ruler defect booked separately. Also confirmed: the owned-bit mask genuinely excludes the crossover bits, no unpack-repack path erases them, and one test parses aeon at a pinned revision, making it a real cross-producer check rather than an author's test.

title: Three dated notes claim aeon's bake does not read the crossover bits; whether that is still true at aeon's current head was not checked.
detail: The notes are dated 2026-08-29 and the seat read aeon only at a pinned revision for the flip maths. If the engine half shipped since, the audit's claim to be the only place a self-mark is noticed is stale. One command against aeon's head settles it. Also tagged: whether any shipped collision file actually carries non-zero unowned bits, which is the data that would make the preservation tests non-vacuous.

title: Deleting the path-escape guards from the main process filesystem module turns no test red, proven by planting it.
detail: CONTROLLER-PROVEN, not predicted: three isRelPathSafe checks neutralised on disk (mutation shown by git diff) and the full suite came back 7624 passed / 8 skipped (7632), byte-identical to the clean baseline the controller measured. Restored from the committed baseline afterwards. rel-path.test.ts tests the guard in isolation; file-io.ts has zero importing tests, verified by two differently-shaped queries with a working control. Seven filesystem primitives cross the process boundary with their guard application asserted by nothing.

title: A header states path-escape safety as an app-wide invariant while the guard is applied at seven of eight handlers, and only one of thirty callers re-checks.
detail: readBinaryFile takes an absolute path deliberately, a designed capability for sheet import reachable only through the loopback-guarded MCP route, and the module says so at file-io.ts:12-14, making this says-unread rather than silent. NOT a vulnerability claim. The finding is the gap between the header sentence and the population: of 30 readBinaryFile call sites exactly one re-checks, and four pass an absolute path with an empty rel operand, one of which passes empty as the BASE path so it resolves against the main process cwd.

title: The sweep that stops a vendored-document list going stale covers only the fixtures tree, so a fourth contract document under src would get no currency check and nothing would say so.
detail: The gate names the hazard in its own words, that a table is a list and a list goes stale silently, and defends against it with two sweeps both rooted at test/fixtures. The three runtime-vendored contract documents under src/core/formats/effects/ are covered by hand-written per-file gates instead. That population has already grown from two to three, so growth is demonstrated rather than hypothetical.

title: The field telling four currency gates which branch to ask is read unguarded, and losing it degrades them to integrity-only while every other row still passes.
detail: branch_that_answers_currency is read with a bare property access on an unchecked JSON.parse in four gates; one reader guards it with a typeof check and a default. No gate asserts the field is present or well-formed. Losing it makes the currency row skip loudly while integrity rows stay green. Mitigating: the re-vendor script updates fields in place and cannot drop it, so the reachable path is a hand-authored sidecar.

title: An adapter interface declares an optional member with no producer and no consumer anywhere.
detail: heightmapsRot appears on exactly one line in the whole tree, its own declaration; the sole caller omits it. Harmless today because nothing reads it; the trap is that a future consumer gets undefined from the only producer with no type error and no test.

title: An IPC channel constant is declared and never registered, exposed or used.
detail: OPEN_PROJECT appears only in its own declaration; the control constant returns four references.

title: Every currency gate asks its question at the producer's tip; none has been pointed at a pinned blob where it would compare a thing to itself.
detail: Eight gates checked one by one: four name origin/master directly, four read the branch from a provenance sidecar, and the ninth is documented at length as asserting integrity rather than currency, with the currency question deliberately delegated elsewhere. THE SEAT NEARLY FILED A FALSE FINDING HERE and caught itself: its first grep over .ts files returned zero for one gate whose tip literal lives in JSON, and four of the eight are invisible to that grep. Also clean: 45 snake_case contract keys checked against their camelCase twins across src with zero collisions, on a sample proven live by three controls.
